programmes.institution: Georgia Institute of Technology (College of Computing / College of Engineering / College of Sciences; School of Computational Science and Engineering)
programmes.programme_name: MS in Computational Science and Engineering (CSE)
programmes.duration: Not stated on the catalogue or CSE pages read (length is expressed as credit hours; typical full-time duration not confirmed)
programmes.credits: 30 US credit hours (12 core + 6 minor-related + 6 non-CS/CSE + 6 course or thesis, per 2026-2027 catalogue)
programmes.entry_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a technical field (CS, mathematics, science or engineering); desired: calculus through multivariable, linear algebra, probability/statistics, 1-2 computing courses and proficiency in a high-level language (C/C++, Python, Java). Missing background may require extra coursework.
programmes.structure_summary: Interdisciplinary MS jointly offered by Computing, Engineering and Sciences. Students pick four of five core courses (numerical linear algebra, CSE algorithms, modelling and simulation, computational data analysis, High Performance Computing), then a specialisation minor with an application area, and finish with either 6 credits of coursework or a defended thesis. HPC is one core option, not mandatory.

core_courses.name: CSE 6140 Computational Science and Engineering Algorithms
CSE 6730 Modeling and Simulation: Foundations and Implementation
CSE/ISYE 6740 Computational Data Analysis: Learning, Mining, and Computation

electives.name: CSE 6230 High Performance Parallel Computing: Tools and Applications
CSE 6644 Iterative Methods for Systems of Equations

programmes.capstone: Either 6 credit hours of approved coursework (course option) or an MS thesis defended before a thesis committee (thesis option).
machines_access: PACE (Partnership for an Advanced Computing Environment): Phoenix cluster and ICE instructional cluster, listed with classroom/teaching resources; use by MS CSE courses not confirmed on the pages read
industry_links: CSE page lists target careers in industry, national laboratories and government contractors (modelling and simulation, HPC, data mining)

programmes.programme_name: Online Master of Science in Computer Science (OMSCS), with HPC/systems electives (CSE 6220, CS 7295, CS 6290, CS 7210)

programmes.entry_requirements: Not read in detail. CSE 6220 suggests prior algorithms course (CS 6515 or undergraduate), C/C++ programming and *nix command-line experience.
programmes.structure_summary: Online CS master requiring one specialisation (15-18 credit hours) plus free electives from any OMSCS course. There is no HPC specialisation, but the catalogue lets a student assemble an HPC/accelerator track: CSE 6220 (parallel algorithms, OpenMP/MPI), CS 7295 (GPU hardware and CUDA), CS 6290 (computer architecture), CS 7210 (distributed computing) and CS 6211 (cloud system design).
